rationale: The CI-fix subsystem already exists and is reached today only by the red-CI-run door (workflow_run -> ci-trigger.ts -> CI_FAILED signal from COMPLETE/PR_DELIVERY -> phases/ci-fix.ts, backed by red-run.ts, ci-diagnosis.ts, check-loop.ts, phases/ci-commit.ts). A maintainer /fix command is a new entry into that existing machinery, not a new subsystem: it adds a SLASH_COMMANDS vocabulary entry plus its COMMAND_SIGNALS/COMMAND_APPLIES rows in commands.ts, a dispatch branch in triggers.ts (with a ciAttempts/maxCiAttempts budget refusal mirroring refuseExhausted/refuseReviews in command-refusals.ts, reusing renderCiExhausted in budget-notices.ts), and either a new TransitionSignal in types.ts with its TRANSITIONS rows in transitions.ts or reuse of CI_FAILED. The one structural seam: discoverFailures in phases/ci-fix.ts reads trigger.runId only when trigger.kind === 'ci', so a comment-triggered fix needs a latest-run-for-branch lookup (github-actions.ts/github.ts) and possibly a widened trigger shape in trigger-events.ts. The workflow's pull-request/issue command arm (.github/workflows/agent-pipeline.yml) must name the command — workflow.test.ts asserts the YAML against SLASH_COMMANDS, and guardrails.test.ts pins the vocabulary order, so both plus commands/triggers/orchestrator/phases/cli/markdown tests are implicated. All of this stays inside the self-contained opencode-agent/ workspace plus its workflow YAML and tests: no papai runtime src/, no SQLite schema or persisted AGENT_STATE shape change beyond (at most) a new signal name (state travels in hidden blocks, not a DB), no chat/task provider surface, no new credentials (the actions:read GITHUB_TOKEN path already exists). Cross-module is false in the papai sense — the change is multi-file but confined to one workspace's command/state-machine/CI-fix modules.
